 Health | 17 minutes ago Govt hospitals offering all dengue tests for free
 says state minister MA Muhit FE REPORT
 Published :
 Nov 18, 2026, 05:10 
 All medical tests for dengue patients are being conducted completely free of charge in the government hospitals across the country, State Minister for Health and Family Welfare Dr. M A Muhit said on Tuesday.
 Additionally, 2,000 doctors have received specialised training to provide dengue treatment.
 The minister said these during the question-answer session in the National Parliament, in response to starred and supplementary questions from lawmakers.
 He mentioned that there are plans to develop community clinics at the grassroots level into "primary healthcare hubs" or one-stop service centres.
 He further emphasised that the government has adopted a "zero-tolerance policy" against illegal clinics and diagnostic centres.
 In response to another question, the state minister said that there are 13,036 sanctioned posts for doctors across all upazila health complexes in the country. Of these, 6,748 positions are currently filled, while 6,288 remain vacant.
 A recruitment process for over 4,000 doctors has already been initiated to fill these vacancies.
 Meanwhile, the number of deaths linked to dengue infections has risen to 507 since January this year as five more patients died in the past 24 hours until 8:00 Tuesday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
 The health authorities also reported 1,537 new cases of hospitalisations due to the mosquito-borne viral disease taking the total caseload to 165,644.
 Of the total hospitalisations this year, 5,609 patients remain in hospitals across the country while the rest returned home after recovery.
 On the other hand, the number of child deaths linked to measles has reached 1,323 as five more children died in the past 24 hours across the country. Of the total fatalities, 105 were confirmed cases, said DGHS bulletin.
 Meanwhile, in the past 24 hours, 1,228 suspected and 86 confirmed measles infections were registered.
 The total number of suspected measles infections rose to 250,797 and confirmed infections to 25,628 since mid-March.
 In response to a measles outbreak rapidly spreading across the country, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has already vaccinated over 20.16 million children since April.
